message.content:
Five clauses to push back on, most dangerous first:

1. Clause 4 (Liability). Your liability is unlimited while the Client is capped at 30 days of fees, so one mistake could cost more than the whole project. Propose: "Each party's total liability is limited to the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim."

2. Clause 3 (Intellectual property). It hands over your pre-existing templates, tools and fonts and bans portfolio use. Propose: "Contractor keeps all pre-existing materials and grants Client a perpetual licence to use them inside the deliverables; Contractor may show the work in a portfolio."

3. Clause 7 (Exclusivity). A worldwide 3-year ban on a whole sector can end your business. Propose: "For 6 months after termination, Contractor will not work for the Client's named direct competitors listed in Annex A."

4. Clause 5 (Renewal). 24-month automatic renewal with 180 days notice by post is a trap. Propose: "Renewal is for 12 months; either party may cancel by email 30 days before expiry."

5. Clauses 2 and 6 (Payment and termination). 120-day payment, a 40% holdback and no pay for work in progress shift all risk to you. Propose: "Invoices are due in 30 days with 1.5% monthly interest; on early termination Client pays for all work performed plus 30% of the remaining fee."

Also negotiate clause 9: each side should bear its own legal costs.
